body:
McVay said he addressed the fourth-quarter exchange with Philadelphia fans and promised the coaching staff will handle high-emotion moments with more composure moving forward

        During a wild week in the NFL, which saw two officials suspended for unprofessional conduct and a head coach penalized for using profanity on the field, we also witnessed assistant coaches and fans go at it in Philly.During the Los Angeles Rams' thrilling, 24-20 comeback victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, some Rams assistant coaches got a little excited in their box and started banging on the glass while also trading some obscene hand gestures with the Philly faithful. At one point, an Eagles fan even threw a drink at the coaches' box. The now-viral interaction allegedly took place after Kyren Williams' game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Check out what happened here:
Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed the incident on Monday, saying, "We'll be better in those situations," per ESPN. "We'll learn from that," McVay said. "We'll be better. Those fans are really into it, but I know that we want to make sure that we're representing the class and just the calm steadiness that we want to have while also being emotionally into it. And there's ways that we can have that reflected.
"We did talk about it, and that won't be an issue moving forward."McVay said he had been in a similar situation earlier in his career, back when he was calling plays for Washington as an assistant coach.  "You get excited and emotional," McVay siad. There was plenty of emotion to be found at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday. The Eagles held a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter, but Nick Sirianni's failed decision to go for the touchdown on a fourth-and-goal from the two-yard line opened the door for a dramatic Rams comeback. Los Angeles then put together two straight 10-play scoring drives, both capped by Williams' touchdowns, to escape Philadelphia with the win. 
This marked Jalen Hurts' first career loss when leading by double digits with five minutes remaining in the game, and Matthew Stafford's first such win with the Rams. It also marked the third time in the Sirianni era where the Eagles blew a 10-point lead at home.

title: Yankees commit four errors in ALDS Game 2 as familiar problem pushes their season to the brink vs. Rays - CBS Sports
description: The Yankees made three of their four errors in the first inning on an ugly night for the New York defense
body:
The Yankees made three of their four errors in the first inning on an ugly night for the New York defense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:05 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sometimes, the game plays to the scouting report. The AL-best Tampa Bay Rays are known for putting pressure on the defense and the New York Yankees are not known for pristine glovework. Both of those traits were on full display in Game 2 of the ALDS on Monday (TB 5, NY 2). New York made three errors and four total defensive mistakes in the first five batters of the game to gift the Rays a 1-0 lead. The Yankees went on to make four total errors in a loss that put them in an 0-2 hole in the best-of-five series.Truth be told, it is a minor miracle the Yankees and presumptive AL Cy Young winner Cam Schlittler escaped that first inning down just one run, and with Schlittler having thrown only 19 pitches. It could have been a much bigger inning for the Rays. 
"I'm not disappointed in our defense," Schlittler said after Game 2. "... Really just disappointed in myself. That's baseball and those things are gonna happen, but I've got to be able to work through those. I wasn't able to do that today"  Here's how the inning played out and how the Rays took advantage of New York's sloppiness.
1st batter: Error on Ryan McMahonFrom a degree of difficulty perspective, this was the most egregious misplay. Yandy Díaz, Tampa's leadoff hitter, smashed a ground ball directly into the Tropicana Field turf that Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon booted. He didn't boot it, really. It was a chest-high hop that McMahon let get by him. This ground ball has to be an out, plain and simple:  
The next batter, Jonathan Aranda, followed with a first-pitch ground ball single by a diving McMahon, who was shaded toward shortstop. That wasn't a defensive misplay. It was just a well-placed grounder. It did put runners at first and second with no outs, though. Three pitches into the game, the pressure was on.   3rd batter: Error on Jazz Chisholm Jr.  For the second straight year, Rays slugger Junior Caminero led the majors in ground ball double plays. He had 26. His ground ball to shortstop in the first inning wasn't going to be a double play because George Lombard Jr. had to range too far to his left to field it, but Jazz Chisholm Jr. forced the throw anyway, and it sailed wide of first base.  
The errant throw allowed Díaz to trot home from third to score Tampa's first run.  
Lombard did good work reaching this ball and flipping it to second, and Chisholm did well to reach for the relay, but the throw was completely unnecessary. Chisholm and every infielder in this position has to know the proper play is holding the ball and taking the out. Instead, a run scored, and Caminero advanced to second with one out.  "Probably a little force there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after the game. "You obviously don't have great speed there going down the line.  Probably best if you're under control and you make the throw, though, it's probably going to be bang-bang.  So I don't necessarily have a problem with the throw.  We've got to play catch.  It's the big leagues."
  4th batter: Error on Austin Wells  With Caminero at second and one out, Schlittler struck out Rays cleanup hitter Liam Hicks, or so he thought. He got Hicks to look at a middle-middle fastball in an 0-2 count, but Hicks took a half-swing that hit catcher Austin Wells in the mitt. Replay confirmed the catcher interference, which is another error, and puts Hicks at first base. From a strikeout to a baserunner.  
Catcher interference is up across baseball because of pitch-framing. Catchers have a tendency to reach forward so they can frame the pitch, and inevitably there's more contact with the catcher's mitt. New York committed seven catcher interferences during the regular season, the second most in baseball. Wells committed four of the seven.    5th batter: Potential double play becomes one out  A lot has to go right to double up Chandler Simpson, baseball's fastest man. He hit into six double plays during the regular season, which really isn't all that many when you consider how many ground balls he hits in general. Things have go almost exactly right to double up Simpson, and it looked like the Yankees had a chance to do exact that in the first inning.  
With Caminero at second and Hicks at first base, Simpson hit a ground ball right to Chisholm at second base, but Chisholm's feed pulled Lombard off the bag at second base. Lombard was able to get back to the bag to get one out, but the poor throw eliminated any chance to turn the inning-ending double play. This is a fielder's choice, not an error, but the poor feed was a bad play.
Schlittler was able to get Victor Mesa Jr. to ground out -- routinely and without any funny business -- to second base to end the inning, stranding Caminero at third and Simpson at first. He had to get six outs in the first inning. Other than the Aranda single, Schlittler got his batters. The Rays hit a bunch of ground balls at infielders, and the Yankees didn't take the outs.  The Yankees finished Game 2 with four errors (Chisholm, Lombard, McMahon, Wells) and several other misplays. Only two of Tampa's five runs were earned. 
Our biggest question coming into this ALDS matchup was will New York's infield be up to the task? The Rays led baseball in bunt hits and were second in infield singles during the regular season. They're going to make you play clean baseball and the Yankees just don't do that. It has been a constant for years, and it again came back to bite them in Game 2 on Monday.  "Obviously, a really rough night to say the least for us," Boone said after Game 2. "We've got to get over it.  We've responded all year to difficult times, and we've got to do that again.  We've got to get ourselves up off the mat."

The NFC South rivals meet Monday night in New Orleans as Michael Penix Jr. and the Falcons look to build on their first win of the season

        In the Week 4 edition of "Monday Night Football," the New Orleans Saints host the Atlanta Falcons.New Orleans is coming off a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders last week that dropped the Saints to 1-2. The Saints turned the ball over four times in the game and were carved up by Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers on the other side of the ball. New Orleans lost running back Travis Etienne to injured reserve in that game as well. The Saints are now looking to rebound at home.Atlanta is coming off its first win of the season, a destruction of the Green Bay Packers in Michael Penix Jr.'s first start of the year. Both Bijan Robinson and Drake London went completely berserk in Green Bay, with 194 yards on the ground and through the air, respectively. The Falcons are looking to get back to .500 after a dreadful start to the year with Cooper Rush filling in under center.Will the Saints bounce back, or will the Falcons make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Saints vs. Falcons liveDate: Monday, Oct. 5 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: Caesars Superdome (New Orleans)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Saints -2.5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Falcons have the ballThe Falcons didn't make a single trip into the red zone in their first two games of the season, and they totaled just 524 yards in those two contests. They then came out in Week 3 and absolutely stomped on the Green Bay defense, piling up 498 yards on "Thursday Night Football" -- 256 through the air and 242 on the ground. They did all that while bouncing back from a game-opening interception by Michael Penix Jr., who was making his first start of the year after returning from his latest knee injury.The New Orleans defense, meanwhile, has been lit up for over 30 points in two of its three games this season -- 31 by the Lions and 35 by the Raiders. The Saints, though, held the Ravens to 17 points in the other game and have dealt with poor opponents' field position in the two games where they got tagged, thanks to a combined seven turnovers by the offense. New Orleans' opponents have begun their average drive on the 34.8-yard line, the third-closest to the end zone of any team in the league.The most fascinating matchup to watch in this one might be the one between Falcons wideout Drake London and Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry. London had just six catches for 80 yards through the first two games of the season with Cooper Rush under center, but he went off for nine catches and 194 yards against Green Bay last week. London has a monster target share in games where Penix has started, and he is clearly the top target for the lefty signal-caller.
McKinstry isn't a corner who just plays one side of the field; his snaps have been split just about equally between left and right cornerback, and I'd probably expect him to follow London whenever he lines up on the perimeter. The Falcons would do well to get London lined up in the slot more often than usual, because McKinstry has yet to play a snap in the slot this season, per Pro Football Focus. Shifting London inside would yield more advantageous matchups.Of course, Atlanta's offense is still based around Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Robinson is averaging a career-best 5.3 yards per carry this season, thanks in large part to his 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns a week ago. The Falcons have been clocked for an average of 4.7 yards per carry on running-back runs, according to Tru Media, the fourth-worst mark in the NFL. When the Saints have the ballTyler Shough led the NFL in completions through the first three weeks of the year. Shough is 91 of 132 (68.9%) for 917 yards (6.9 per attempt), eight touchdowns and three interceptions so far. He's done most of his work in second halves as the Saints have worked to come back from deficits: he's just 32 of 53 for 278 yards, two touchdowns and an interception before the break, while he's 59 of 79 for 639 yards, six touchdowns and two picks after it. 
The Falcons rank a surprising first in the league in pressure rate so far this season, generating a sack, hit or hurry on 45.2% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media. They were expected to have one of the worst pass rushes in the NFL coming into the year in the absence of both Jalon Walker (injury) and James Pearce Jr. (suspension), but instead, guys like Gervon Dexter (10), Brandon Dorlus (eight), Cameron Thomas (eight) and Samson Ebukam (seven) have been getting after it up front. The Saints haven't had much in the way of success running the ball, and will be without Travis Etienne hereafter, as he went on injured reserve. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are expected to share the load in the backfield with Etienne out, though CJ Donaldson could mix in as well. Kamara has been extremely inefficient on the ground for several years now, but he's at least a threat as a pass-catcher. Miller has only 140 carries in his career and has averaged south of 4.0 yards per attempt.PredictionThe Falcons looked much improved last week against the Packers, thanks in large part to the return of Michael Penix Jr. They hadn't even entered the red zone through the first two weeks of the season, then dropped 35 points on the Packers in Week 3. The Saints, meanwhile, could conceivably be 3-0 right now if not for backbreaking turnovers. They have two one-possession losses, both in games where they turned it over at least three times. If they can avoid giving the ball to the Falcons, I think they can win a close one here.  Prediction: Saints 23, Falcons 20

title: Tyquan Thornton to have surgery after ankle injury; 'chance' Chiefs' WR could return this season, per insider - CBS Sports

        Tests on Monday revealed that Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton will need surgery after dislocating his ankle during Kansas City's Week 4 game against the Raiders, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The expected time for recovery is between three and four months, but there is a "small chance" of a late-season return, Zenitz reports. The Chiefs' wideout suffered a left ankle injury after making a 55-yard catch late in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Thornton initially didn't know that he had suffered an injury after making the catch. He began celebrating his big play before he realized what had happened. Cameras initially showed the severity of Thornton's injury, but then immediately stopped showing any replays. Thornton received an air cast to get off the field.It was later revealed that Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors. A full evaluation on Monday morning revealed surgery is necessary. While the injury is tough news for the 4-0 Chiefs, Zenitz added that "it's a relatively positive outlook" for Kansas City. A return toward the end of the season or during the playoffs is still possible.
Thornton's injury occurred after he had a monster day. He caught five passes for 111 yards and two scores. Thornton entered the game with six catches for 108 yards. The 50th overall pick in the 2022 draft, Thornton spent his first three seasons with the Patriots before joining the Chiefs in 2025. He set career highs last season with 438 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 23.1 yards per catch. 
Thornton's teammates made sure that his 55-yard catch would not go in vain. Kenneth Walker III scored one play later and scored again less than 20 seconds later after the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. 
Kansas City prevailed, 30-27, improving to 4-0 and handing the Raiders their first loss of the season. Walker rumbled for 177 yards and two scores and was again a key contributor in a Chiefs win. The Chiefs wouldn't have beaten the Raiders without Thornton, however. "First off, I'm just praying for him," Patrick Mahomes told CBS Sports lead sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson afterward. "You never want anyone to get injured, and you're hoping it's better than it looked out there. Praying for him, and hopefully he comes back healthy."  
With Thornton injured, the Chiefs will have to lean more on their other playmakers, which include Walker, Xavier Worthy, Travis Kelce, and Rashee Rice, who missed the majority of Sunday's game after injuring his hamstring in the second quarter. The Chiefs will have time to rest and recover during their Week 5 bye before hosting the winless Chargers in Week 6.

        The NFL suspended line judge Jeff Seeman two games for "unprofessional conduct" toward Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride in Week 4. The harshest he got was, 'You're ruining the game.'" Ironically, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was penalized after saying something similar to an official during New England's win over the Buffalo Bills. The penalty helped set up a Buffalo touchdown. "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said afterward. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him.         San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw faced his former team, the Denver Broncos, on Sunday and used it as a chance to make his feelings on his old coach known. Greenlaw played for the Broncos, and head coach Sean Payton, last season. While his time there was short, it was impactful, just not for the right ways if you ask the LB.Greenlaw said something to Payton during the game and appeared to tell the head coach, "Hey! You get the f-ck off my field!" after San Fran's 24-14 home victory over Denver. The 29-year-old didn't try to backtrack, later confirming his comments while speaking to the media."I told him to get the f--k off the field," Greenlaw said of his postgame comments, per the San Francisco Chronicle. "That's it: 'Get the f--k off the field.'"He signed a three-year, $35 million contract with the Broncos ahead of the 2025 season and in his one year in Denver, Greenlaw played in eight games, starting seven. His missed time was due to a one-game suspension and injuries, something Greenlaw credits for the downfall of his relationship with his HC. Greenlaw said Payton stopped talking to him in Week 12, believing it was over the lingering injury. 
"He definitely was, for sure," Greenlaw said, when asked if he thought Payton was ignoring him because the head coach was frustrated on Denver's return on their investment. "He would walk by - I would walk by - and he wouldn't even look at me because of my injury. So I just knew what it was (with him) there."After Sunday's win, Greenlaw said he hadn't talked to Payton "in months" adding it dates back to when he was on the team."It's just a lot," Greenlaw said.
Greenlaw had 43 total tackles, a sack and a forced fumble and an interception in 2025. He finished with four tackles in their divisional win over the Buffalo Bills and and six tackles in their AFC Championship loss to the New England Patriots, which would end up being his last game in orange.
The premature release was another thing Greenlaw was upset about. "The disrespect," Greenlaw said regarding his motivation was for Sunday comments. "He couldn't be man-to-man and call my phone and say, 'We're going to cut you.'"Payton was asked about the two exchanges and kept his answer politically correct."I think the world of him. I love everything about him," Payton said. "He plays with that emotion and so, all good."
Greenlaw seemed to use the motivation for his own good, leading the team with 12 tackles, marking his most so far this season.The 49ers now sit at 4-0 and will face the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field next week. Campbell replied to Tyson's comments on social media and credited coaching more than anything.
There is some truth in Campbell's response. Just look at what happened to Florida State when it tried to make splashy transfer portal additions in 2024. On the other hand, it's hard to win with an underfunded roster. Review our college football spending tiers at 247Sports, and it's hard to find winning programs toward the bottom.

title: 2027 Fantasy baseball catcher preview: Gabriel Moreno's breakout fuels optimism - CBS Sports
description: The catcher position took the big collective step forward we were all hoping for in 2026, and then they all mostly took a big step back.
body:
The catcher position took the big collective step forward we were all hoping for in 2026, and then they all mostly took a big step back. At the All-Star break, six different catchers had at least an .800 OPS while logging at least 200 at-bats; in the second half, five catchers had at least an .800 OPS in at least 150 at-bats, but only Gabriel Moreno actually managed it across both halves of the season. Here's how those six first-half breakouts fared in the second:Ben Rice | NYY – First half: .971 | Second half: .791Hunter Goodman | COL – First half: .863 OPS | Second half: .794Dillon Dingler | DET – First half: ..31 | Second half: .630Liam Hicks | TB  – First half: .822 | Second half: .769Gabriel Moreno | ARI – First half: .822 | Second half: .927Shea Langeliers | ATH – First half: .807 | Second half: .778**missed much of the second half with a knee injuryFor the most part, they didn't totally collapse. And this list notably doesn't include Drake Baldwin, whose first-half numbers were dragged down by a miserable few weeks right after he came back from an oblique injury; he had a big second half, finishing third at the position in OPS. But when it looked like we were getting a whole new crop of potential superstars early on, that momentum didn't quite carry over for the whole season.Add it all up, and we ended up with 11 players worth at least $10 on the FanGraphs.com Player Rater, actually down from the 12 who hit that mark in 2025. But that doesn't quite paint the right picture either, because the number of $20 catchers actually jumped from four in 2025 to nine in 2026, and Langeliers would have gotten there if not for his injury. Despite a somewhat disappointing second half across the board, the position did take a big step forward overall.We're going to give some of that back, of course, because it just doesn't look like Rice is ever going to have catcher eligibility ever again, while Dingler and Hicks feel like tough bets to repeat their overall success. Even with that, catcher does at least look stronger than it has at the high end in a long time, and that's without assuming a bounce back from Cal Raleigh. You might still find the pickings kind of slim in 2027 drafts if you play in a two-catcher league, but there are enough capable catchers that getting one of the best ones doesn't necessarily put you way ahead of most of the league. 
And this isn't just a one-year trend, as the (relative) resurgence of the catcher position started in 2025. The top names at the position are mostly young enough that we should expect them to at least hold steady for the next few years – obviously, you can't always bet on that, especially with catchers, but there aren't a ton of glaring red flags at the top of the position. Catcher certainly isn't the strongest position in Fantasy. Pound for pound, it might still be the weakest, even. But that gap has shrunk over the past few years, and with some really exciting young players on the verge of establishing themselves in the majors, it could get even better in 2027. It's okay to be optimistic about the state of catchers right now! 2026 Catcher Review Ben Rice, NYY: .264 - 105 - 41 - 97 - 3Hunter Goodman, COL: .245 - 84 - 41 - 88 - 5Drake Baldwin, ATL: .284 - 85 - 25 - 79 - 3Gabriel Moreno, ARI: .311 - 72 - 16 - 83 - 6William Contreras, MIL: .270 - 82 - 18 - 94 - 1Dillon Dingler, DET: .243 - 72 - 27 - 91 - 0Liam Hicks, TBR: .284 - 66 - 18 - 82 - 3Carter Jensen, KCR: .239 - 80 - 27 - 81 - 2Iván Herrera, STL: .241 - 98 - 19 - 69 - 8Shea Langeliers, ATH: .262 - 58 - 23 - 58 - 3Salvador Perez, KCR: .229 - 50 - 21 - 78 - 1Carson Kelly, CHC: .258 - 57 - 10 - 58 - 0Some of these names aren't surprising at all. Rice, Goodman, Baldwin, Langeliers, and Contreras all more or less did what was expected of them (or more), and Jensen and Herrera were extremely popular breakout candidates who mostly lived up to expectations. If you avoided the Cal Raleigh landline, paying up for a premier catcher was a pretty good idea in 2027.
The more interesting names here are the ones we didn't really see coming. Moreno and Dingler had very mild breakout hype, but were definitely overshadowed by some of the other names involved. But nobody had Hicks as a high-priority target coming into the season. He has always had elite contact skills, and those remained in 2026. What changed? Well, he started making a little bit of damage on contact. Not a ton more, but he started angling the ball to the more beneficial parts of the field (in the air, to the pull side) and that was enough to lead to the breakout. When you look under the hood, Hicks looks like largely the same guy — .319 xwOBA compared to a .313 mark in 2025 — but that combination of his elite contact skills and marginal optimization of his swing had a huge impact. I don't expect that impact to fully carry over to 2027, but I will note that he did finish the season with a .330 xwOBA over his final 250 plate appearances, much of which came during his time with the Rays. Therefore, it's possible they were able to unlock another half-gear or so, though I'm skeptical there's another level here. Hicks should be looked at as a good bet for batting average, and if you hope for 2 homers, you shouldn't end up too disappointed.  	Biggest Breakout from 2026Ben Rice, Yankees Rice had the breakout everyone was hoping for and then some, and probably would have been a top-10 overall hitter even if he wasn't catcher eligible. He won't be for 2027, and I suspect this will end up going down as his best Fantasy season when it's all said and done. But since his eligibility won't carry over, let's take a second to talk about someone else: Gabriel Moreno, DiamondbacksMoreno has always been viewed as someone with another gear he could hit, and after showing flashes of it in 2025, he fully broke out in 2026. He did that despite a pretty quiet first half, where he hit .301 but with little production beyond that. The power showed up in the second half, as he clubbed 10 homers after the break, eclipsing his full-season career-high by one just in that span. He probably overperformed a bit on his way to his final numbers (.380 wOBA vs. a .363 expected mark). However, his combination of strong contact skills, at least above-average raw power, and improved pulled-air skills makes it relatively easy to buy in. I don't think this is a situation where I expect the huge second half to lead to another level, but a 15-homer catcher who actively helps you in batting average has plenty of appeal. 
 	Biggest Bust from 2026Cal Raleigh, Mariners He wasn't just the biggest bust at the position in 2026: Raleigh was one of the biggest busts in Fantasy history. It took a big closing kick (12 homers in August and September) for Raleigh to even get to one-third of his homer total from 2025, and he managed to hit below the Mendoza Line in four of six months. Multiple oblique injuries surely didn't help, but as he enters his 30s, it's not like Raleigh is necessarily a safe bet to be healthier moving forward. I expect a big bounce back in 2027, though more to his pre-2025 levels, when he was an elite source of power and counting stats, but a big drag on your batting average. He's still a top-12 catcher for next season, but he might never be the clear top choice again.  	Biggest rankings movers from 2026 to 2027Up: Gabriel Moreno, Diamondbacks; Dillon Dingler, Tigers; Leo Bernal, CardinalsFor a while there, it looked like Dingler was a sure thing to be drafted as a top-six catcher in 2027; now I'm pretty certain he won't be. Still, he's obviously going to be one of the biggest risers after being drafted as the 20th catcher on average coming into the season. Despite how his season ended, Dingler still finished with 27 homers and 91 RBI, big numbers for any position and positively huge numbers for a catcher. There's a catch-22 there, where the big numbers are at least in part because of his huge role in the Tigers' offense, which might also explain why he faded down the stretch. I wouldn't mind seeing the Tigers spell Dingler more with Eduardo Valencia in 2027, and he should very much be on your sleepers list for position after showing enough upside as a rookie to garner regular DH time. There's some irony in the fact that the Cardinals have been desperately searching for their long-term replacement for Yainer Molina while also emerging as perhaps the premier catcher development team in the majors. Ivan Herrera is already a huge developmental win, even if he probably isn't a catcher in the long run, and Jimmy Crooks still looks like a solid long-term option despite an iffy MLB debut. But Bernal looks like the real deal, to the point where Rainiel Rodriguez, arguably the top catching prospect in baseball, is going to take reps at third base this offseason. It's an embarrassment of riches, and Bernal emerged as the team's primary catcher down the stretch, starting every game after his promotion from Triple-A while hitting .284/.333/.474 with excellent underlying metrics and solid defense. He wasn't quite that good at Triple-A and probably has some regression coming for him, but this is a solid all-around skill set that should lead to plenty of playing time and 20-plus homer potential for 2027. He's already your favorite Fantasy analyst's favorite breakout pick at the position. 
Down: Cal Raleigh, Mariners; Adley Rutschman, Red Sox; Yainer Diaz, Astros; Agustin Ramirez, MarlinsAnother frustrating, injury-riddled season for Rutschman, who looked like he might be re-emerging as an impact player early on before putting together yet another underwhelming season. Injuries certainly played their part, but we're talking about a soon-to-be 29-year-old catcher who hasn't really been a must-start Fantasy option since 2023. It's not impossible that we get a bounce-back season out of Rutschman, but we're done giving him the benefit of the doubt because he was good for two seasons at the start of his career.And, honestly, ditto for Diaz. He finished with decent enough numbers thanks to a big second half, but given how inconsistent he has been over the past few years, I need to see more than that before I view him as a top-12 catcher again. That upside is there thanks to his strong contact skills and bat speed, but his poor swing decisions too often lead him to swing at the wrong pitches, subsequently minimizing his production. That streakiness is probably inherent to his skill set, especially since he doesn't really have any way of impacting the game when hits aren't dropping in. As a high-upside No. 2 catcher, Diaz still has some appeal, but at this point, I think he can be pretty safely ignored in points leagues. 
And then there's Ramirez, whose limitations were just completely exposed this season. The plus raw power was still there, thanks to near-elite bat speed, but there were just too many holes in his swing to get to that power often enough. He swings and misses too often, and when he does make contact, too much of it is either hit hard into the ground or sky high into the air, and you won't find much production on either end of that spectrum. The Marlins also soured on his defense behind the plate, so when he returned from the minors, he was mostly used as a DH. If he can hit well enough to justify that spot, it's actually not a bad thing for his value. Ramirez just didn't show the kind of consistent impact to justify an everyday role at the most demanding offensive position. The upside for 20-plus homers and useful speed is still there, but you can't go into 2027 expecting it. To be honest, I'm not sure if we can even go into 2027 expecting him to have a big role with the Marlins; he'll likely have to earn that with a strong offseason and Spring Training performance at this point. Offseason preview  	Who needs an upgrade most?  RedsGiantsRangersGuardiansPhilliesThe Phillies are probably in the toughest spot of any team because J.T. Realmuto looks like he's in free fall in the first year of a three-year contract. They could really use an upgrade, but I'm not sure how likely they are to pursue it, given how expensive their team already is. Otherwise, there aren't a ton of contenders who really need an upgrade at catcher. The Guardians could always use a better stick behind the plate, but they seem content to punt on offense in favor of the best possible defense they can manage back there. 
The team that feels likeliest to make a big swing at catcher this offseason is probably the Giants, who are run by Buster Posey and who clearly weren't happy with what they were getting from the position this season. Of course, given what we've seen from this front office, do you really want to see what the Giants do when they are "desperate?" I would guess they'll try to make a big impact there, though the Giants might be best served by punting in 2027 and doing a soft reset, given how many pitcher injuries they'll be dealing with. As for the Reds: With Alfredo Duno reaching (and holding his own at) Double-A as a 20-year-old, the Reds aren't likely to be looking for a long-term answer at catcher this offseason, despite it being an area they could stand to upgrade.  	Top impending free agents Ryan JeffersTyler StephensonCarson KellyJonah HeimUnfortunately, if you're looking for an upgrade at catcher, the pickings are quite slim on the free agent market. Jeffers looked like he was having a breakout, but he posted just a .230/.316/.406 line after the All-Star break, with the underlying numbers to back it up. He's not a bad option, but he's probably not much better than just a middle-of-the-pack option at the position, and the same goes for Stephenson. Getting a middle-of-the-pack producer at catcher would still be an upgrade for a few of these teams, but nobody on the free agent marketplace looks likely to change any teams' outlook. 
 	Trade candidates Hunter GoodmanIvan HerreraYainer DiazKeibert RuizSean MurphyThere is always a lot of speculation with these kinds of predictions, but I wouldn't be surprised to see any of these names moved. The Rockies were reportedly at least listening to offers for Goodman, but they needed to be absolutely blown away at the deadline and the same likely remains true coming off a 41-homer season. He isn't a great defender, but he is passable and is only set to make a few million dollars in arbitration this season, so every team looking for an upgrade should be in on Goodman if the Rockies make him available.The same is true of Herrera, who probably shouldn't be a full-time catcher but whose bat is absolutely good enough to play first base or DH or any other position you think he might be able to handle. The Cardinals have at least two viable young options at catcher, even beyond Herrera and have arguably the top catching prospect in baseball with an ETA as early as 2027. Herrera is coming off a .241/.353/.382 line and I think it's reasonable to at least expect a bit more power from him moving forward. As a DH who can handle backup catcher duties, this is a profile that should garner a ton of trade interest around the league.Diaz has flopped ever since his breakout, but there remains at least theoretical upside here – he makes a lot of contact and tends to hit the ball hard despite pretty terrible plate discipline overall. The Astros have quietly become a pretty poor player development team over the past few years, so some smart team might view Diaz as a nice buy-low option in the right offseason program. The Astros would have to decide their .500 record despite winning the AL West, plus their unceremonious (and acrimonious) exit from the playoffs is a sign that they are far enough away from competing that Diaz isn't worth what will likely still be a pretty reasonable salary in arbitration. There's no guarantee owner/acting GM Jim Crane will be interested in pursuing that path. But he should be.
 	Top 2027 rookies to know Leo Bernal, CardinalsEthan Salas, PadresRainiel Rodriguez, CardinalsAlfredo Duno, RedsVahn Lackey, TwinsCaden Bodine, Rays Thayron Liranzo, TigersBlake Mitchell, RoyalsRamon Ramirez, RoyalsJosue Briceno, TigersOwen Ayers, CubsCooper Ingle, GuardiansSalas made his MLB debut as a 20-year-old, and in fact won't even turn 21 until next June. He re-emerged as a top prospect with 10 homers and 17 steals in 96 games between the top two levels of the minors. While he has mostly struggled to make an impact in the majors, he has been used as a starter already in the playoffs and seems like he'll have a starting job waiting for him on Opening Day. The combination of power, speed, and plate discipline, plus Salas' unusually precocity, makes him a very high-upside option in the long run. With that said, growing pains will likely be a part of the profile, too.Rodriguez and Duno both bring unusual raw power to the plate and both more than held their own as very young players at Double-A. At this point, it looks like a long shot that either will be on the Opening Day roster, but both are talented enough that you can't dismiss the possibility out of hand.

Gleason's blocked punt was a pivotal moment for both the city of New Orleans and himself. Now, 20 years later, he opened up on 'Good Morning America' about his own 'rebirth'

        The parallels between Steve Gleason's legendary blocked punt, what it meant for the city of New Orleans and how it resembles his own personal struggle are chilling. A play on the football field that will forever be known as the "rebirth" of New Orleans was, in many ways, a "rebirth" for Gleason. He just did not know it at the time.Almost exactly 20 years ago, the New Orleans Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time since Hurricane Katrina devastated the city. The venue that served as a shelter for thousands during and after the storm became, once again, the home of a proud football team. A minute and a half after the opening kickoff of the Sept. 25, 2006, game against the rival Atlanta Falcons, Gleason made the most memorable play in franchise history, blocking a punt that was scooped up in the end zone. It was a play that gave the Saints and the city of New Orleans hope once again.
On Monday, the Falcons return to the Superdome to face the Saints in Week 4 of the 2026 season.  The team will honor Gleason and that 2006 squad in a 20th anniversary celebration.It will undoubtedly be a meaningful return to the Superdome for Gleason."When I roll back into that stadium, I will not only be revisiting a monument of 2006, but I will be walking into a mirror — a place that had to learn how to rise," Gleason said on "Good Morning America" on Monday. "I had to learn the same thing."
Steve Gleason's battle with ALS after football careerFive years after he made an indelible mark on New Orleans with his blocked punt, in 2011, Gleason revealed that he was diagnosed with ALS. The average life expectancy after diagnosis is about three to five years, yet Gleason is among the 10-20% of those who survive for 10 years or more."I'm still here," Gleason said on GMA. "That still surprises some people. It does not surprise me as much as it used to."Gleason uses speech synthesis technology to communicate and requires assistance to move and breathe. Still, he relishes in a "miraculous, wonderful life" and remains an active contributor to the ALS awareness movement. He became the first NFL player to win a Congressional Gold Medal in 2019 for his activism.
NFL players represent one of the populations that is at higher risk of developing ALS than the general public, Gleason said. He found community with other football players who battled or are currently battling the disease, including Chris Johnson, Tim Shaw, O.J. Brigance, Eric Stevens, and Steve Smith.What "Rebirth" means to GleasonThat game 20 years ago did not just revive the city of New Orleans. In hindsight, it was a pivotal moment in Gleason's life. It just took a few years for him to fully realize what it would mean to be a central figure in a defining moment in the city's and the football team's history."If I do not block that punt, I am another former special teams player, a has-been football guy," Gleason said. "When ALS came, I probably fade away quietly and die anonymously. That play made me visible at the exact moment this city needed a symbol. Years later, that visibility became a lifeline. So many people have told us our foundation's work saved their lives."
Last week, Gleason announced that he will release a musical album. The project combines his poetry with the instrumental talent of local musicians in New Orleans. He has already released two tracks and will continue to unveil more throughout the month of October. The songs are largely influenced by Gleason's life since his ALS diagnosis.Fittingly, the album is titled "Rebirth.""The truth I have to live with is this: The same play that helped New Orleans breathe again," Gleason said, "is a big reason I'm still breathing now."How Gleason remembers his blocked puntGleason, a special teams stalwart, ran unblocked to deflect the Falcons' punt into the end zone, where Curtis Deloatch recovered the loose ball for a touchdown. The crowd popped when Gleason made contact with the ball, rivaling that of any big play in football history. It was a cathartic moment for a city that, over the previous year, had been through misery.
For the first time in a year, New Orleans had something to cheer about."During the Falcons' first two games of the year, we noticed a lot of confusion and errors on their punt team, so we wanted to exploit that," Gleason said, recounting the preparation for that contest. "The scheme is an interior stunt where I cross from the right A gap to the left A gap. Sure enough, the Falcons had some confusion on their assignments. Because they used the slide technique, I ended up unblocked and the B gap opened up for me."At that point, there wasn't much thinking. All the film study, repetition and technique took over. The gap opened, and I knew I had a real chance. Then the ball hit my hands."The Saints had spent the past year bouncing from stadium to stadium because of the damage Hurricane Katrina had done to the Superdome. They went 3-13 in that adversity-filled campaign. Questions arose about whether the franchise would return to the Superdome or to New Orleans in general.
But after a year of repairs to the facility, the Saints made their way back to the Superdome and dominated their division rival. The blocked punt helped the Saints down the Falcons 23-3 in a game that was symbolic of New Orleans' revival as a city.In turn, a statue of that blocked punt stands outside the Superdome.

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers     There are a number of different wagering options available on each race, and here we will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that help clarify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.           Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds           Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.             What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.            The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                     Win           The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                      Place           The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.            Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                       Show           A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                       Win/Place           Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                       Place/Show           The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                       Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)            Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.            It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                       The most popular horse racing bet types           Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).            It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.           Exactas           An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                       Trifectas           This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.            The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                       Superfectas           Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                      Super High 5           Some books will even allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                      Box           A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.            For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:           $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:           $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.            A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                       How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers           While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                       Daily Double           The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.            Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                       Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6           Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.           Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.            The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                       Understanding horse racing payouts           After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.            The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:           2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								           				           $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				           If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.            For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:            2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				          Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting          The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.           October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes           Triple Crown of horse racing           The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.            Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.            The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                       Tips and advice for betting on horse racing           There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                       Racing forms and past performances           These are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                       Track conditions           Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                       Horse tendencies            From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.            The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                       Post position           Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                      Trainer and jockey information           A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                       Workout times           There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                       Speed figures           Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.            Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                      Manage your horse racing betting bankroll           Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                       Rules and responsible gaming           Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.           Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.           FAQHow to bet on horse racing?There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.How to bet on horse racing online?Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.What is a box bet in horse racing?A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.What is a show bet in horse racing?A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.What is a key box bet in horse racing?A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

        The NFL suspended referee Adrian Hill one game for "unprofessional conduct" toward Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson in Week 4. The ruling came after the league reviewed a play from the Vikings' 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in which Wilson and Hill collided.Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, the referee stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson. It appeared that the referee took exception to the inadvertent collision and blamed Wilson, while Wilson pointed at Gordon and said that it was the Dolphins player who initiated the contact.A second official stepped in to separate Wilson from the referee after they exchanged words and pointed in opposite directions. The referee appeared to be instructing Wilson to return to his side of the field.
This is not the only play involving an official and a player that raised eyebrows on Sunday. The NFL also reviewed an interaction between official Jeff Seeman and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. McBride pleaded for a pass interference penalty, to which the official appeared to deliver a profane response. That incident prompted a response from NFL Players Association president JC Tretter and a two-game suspension for Seeman."This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel also had a heated moment with an official over a pass interference situation. Vrabel was said to have told a down judge that he made "a f---ing terrible call," which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Vrabel called the official "a little sensitive" for issuing the flag.
